objective: Independent verifier attack on C02's 18-vertex obstruction and 18+12q family, plus an explicitly uncompiled Lean formalization path; no root closure or admission.

atomic_claims.text: A fresh standard-library implementation scans all 4,686,825 nine-edge subsets of the labeled 18-vertex C02 graph, finds exactly 26 perfect matchings and zero divisible complementary 2-factors, with spectra counts 6,4,16 as recorded.
The same independent implementation checks all 172 deletions of at most two vertices and the displayed noninduced P3-factor for the labeled 18-vertex graph.
Dropping the bipartite right-brick hypothesis is unsound: the Petersen/Petersen three-sum control has a spanning (9,9) 2-factor. This attacks only that overgeneralization, not C02.

A line-by-line audit of the general 18+12q construction found no contradiction; the bipartition degree-sum argument gives exactly two selected boundary edges and the explicit P3 partition has the required order arithmetic.
Lean files specify arithmetic endpoints, exhaustive local five-cycle certificates and the intended Mathlib semantics, but were not compiled and do not prove FamilyTarget or RootProblem.

assumptions: Finite simple graphs; cubic means every vertex has degree three and 3-connected means vertex connectivity at least three.
P3 is a selected two-edge path on three distinct vertices and need not be induced.
The C02 family uses a bipartite right brick; the independent negative control shows this hypothesis cannot simply be removed.
Allowed axioms remain finite-graph-basic and finite-combinatorics; no new axiom or verifier identity is admitted.
risks: The finite exhaustive replay concerns the single labeled 18-vertex witness, not a graph-order census or a proof of minimum obstruction order.
The all-q family audit is mathematical prose plus bounded parameter checks; the full family has no Lean kernel receipt.
The producing environment had no Lean executable; Local.lean and MathlibTargets.lean are uncompiled drafts and may require API or proof repairs.
Global restriction/embedding, closed-component transfer, all-q connectivity, explicit P3 bijection and matching-complement bridges remain open formalization obligations.
C02 separates the stronger divisible-two-factor assertion from the root; it neither proves nor refutes the root problem.
CI, content hashes and transport checks are not mathematical admission.
